subject: spanish
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How do you say “I have to do a lot of homework”?
options: Tengo que hacer muchas tareas domésticas
questions.explain: “Los deberes” = homework and “tengo que hacer” = I have to do.
'La asignatura' is a false friend: it means 'school subject', not 'signature' (which is 'la firma').

questions.q: How do you say 'I live in a quiet neighbourhood'?
questions.explain: 'El barrio' is masculine, so 'tranquilo' agrees; 'vivo' is the correct first-person form.
“Mixto” = mixed, so “el colegio mixto” = “a co-educational school” (boys and girls).
'Embarazada' is a classic false friend: it means 'pregnant', not 'embarrassed' (which is 'avergonzado/a').
“El barrio” means “the neighbourhood/district”.

questions.q: How do you say “My favourite subject is geography”?
options: Mi asignatura preferida es la historia
Mi asignatura preferida es la geografía
Mi firma preferida es la geografía
Mi asignatura aburrida es la geografía
questions.explain: “Asignatura preferida” = favourite subject and “la geografía” = geography.

questions.q: Which sentence means “Classes start at nine o'clock”?
options: Las clases terminan a las nueve
La clase empiezan a las nueve
Las clases empiezan a las diez
Las clases empiezan a las nueve
questions.explain: “Empezar” = to start and “a las nueve” = at nine o'clock.
“La asignatura” means “a school subject”; it is a false friend with “signature” (la firma).
“La pizarra” means “the board/whiteboard” in the classroom.

questions.q: How do you say “There isn't much to do in my village”?
options: No hay mucho que hago en mi pueblo
No hay nada de hacer en mi ciudad
No hay mucho que hacer en mi pueblo
Hay mucho que hacer en mi pueblo
questions.explain: “No hay mucho que hacer” = “there isn't much to do” and “mi pueblo” = “my village”.

questions.q: Which means “The rules are very strict”?
questions.explain: “Las normas” = the rules and “estrictas” = strict.

questions.q: How do you say “We wear a uniform”?
questions.explain: “Llevar” = “to wear” and “llevamos” = “we wear”, so “Llevamos uniforme”.
“Equilibrada” = balanced, so “una dieta equilibrada” = “a balanced diet”.
“La fiebre” means “fever/temperature”, so “tengo fiebre” = “I have a fever”.
'El tabaquismo' is the habit/addiction of smoking, not a shop (that would be 'el estanco').
“El horario” means “the timetable/schedule”, e.g. of lessons or work shifts.

questions.q: How do you say “I live on the third floor”?
options: Vivo en la tercera planta baja
questions.explain: “Tercer” shortens before a masculine noun, so “el tercer piso” = “the third floor”.
“Estar en forma” means “to be fit / in good shape”.

questions.q: How do you say “My town is quite lively”?
questions.explain: “Animada” = lively and a permanent characteristic uses “ser”: “Mi ciudad es bastante animada”.
“La planta baja” means “the ground floor”.
“Las afueras” means “the outskirts” of a town, where many people live.
